item.title: Saudi Arabia seeks access to foreign strategic oil reserves for Aramco
item.description: Aramco CEO Amin Nasser said Saudi Arabia's Energy Ministry is discussing access to government-held oil storage abroad as Houthi attacks on key infrastructure raise concerns over supply disruptions ...
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded: By Salma El Wardany Saudi Arabia is in talks with foreign governments to give state-owned Aramco access to their strategic oil storage, as the kingdom seeks to make its supplies to customers more resilient during disruptions, Chief Executive Officer Amin Nasser said. The move follows a flurry of attacks by Yemen’s Houthis on key Saudi infrastructure, including drone strikes that shut down its most important pipeline for several days in September. On Wednesday, attacks on Aramco’s Shaybah oil field and Dammam airport each killed two people, according to Saudi authorities.  Brent crude climbed above $112 a barrel on Thursday as the violence heightened concerns about further disruptions to Saudi supplies.   “Commercial storage available through partners is limited. The larger capacity lies in what we call strategic storage owned by governments,” Nasser said in an interview with Al Arabiya on Thursday. “The Ministry of Energy is working with its counterparts in other countries to make strategic storage available for Aramco.” The company already holds commercial oil storage in South Korea, Japan, the Netherlands and Egypt’s Mediterranean export hub of Sidi Kerir. “We have maintained these overseas inventories for many years, but we are working to expand them, particularly in Asia,” Nasser said. Aramco wants to double its overseas capacity, Nasser said, without giving a timetable for the expansion or disclosing current capacity. The push forms part of a broader effort to reinforce Saudi Arabia’s infrastructure and export options during the regional crisis. Aramco currently has three main export corridors — the Strait of Hormuz, the Red Sea and Bab el-Mandeb, and Sidi Kerir on the Mediterranean. The conflict prompted the company to begin engineering studies to increase its capacity to move crude from the Persian Gulf in the east to the Red Sea in the west to 10 million barrels a day from 7 million, alongside work on other routes, Nasser said. “We did not wait for the crisis to end,” Nasser said. Building resilience requires “decades of investment and preparation.”

item.title: From SBI to ICICI: Major banking data breaches, cyberattacks in India
item.description: SBI's latest disclosure of exposed customer records adds to a history of cyber incidents affecting Indian banks ...
item.dc:creator: Barkha Mathur
item.content:encoded: State Bank of India (SBI), the country’s largest lender, is investigating a data leak after identifying 3,897 customer records containing personally identifiable information among records found on the dark web. In a stock exchange disclosure on Wednesday, the bank said the source and extent of the exposure were still being investigated. The incident is the latest in a growing number of cyber security breaches involving Indian banks and their technology providers. Some incidents exposed personal information, while others enabled fraudulent withdrawals or disrupted payment services. Here are some of the major cases that exposed vulnerabilities in India’s banking systems recently. 1. SBI data exposure: October 2026 SBI received alerts on October 16 from its threat intelligence provider, the Defence Cyber Agency and the Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) about suspected customer data exposure. A preliminary examination of around 375,000 records found on the dark web identified 3,897 customer records containing personally identifiable information. The data reportedly included names, mobile numbers, dates of birth, email and residential addresses, customer identification details and metadata associated with loan records. SBI said it has activated its cyber incident response and containment protocols and engaged an independent CERT-In-empanelled cybersecurity agency to investigate the incident. The bank said the breach does not have any material impact on the bank’s core business operations, financial performance or business continuity 2. Bank of Baroda: July 2026 Bank of Baroda disclosed a cybersecurity incident involving business email compromise, according to its exchange filing dated July 27. The dataset was advertised on a dark-web site as containing more than 700GB of information, based on an analysis of the site’s metadata, according to media reports. The bank initiated a forensic investigation and said the incident was not expected to have a material impact on its operations, financial performance or business continuity. 3. ICICI Bank ransomware claim: January 2025 and April 2024 The BASHE ransomware and cyber extortion group claimed in January 2025 that it had breached ICICI Bank and threatened to release data unless its demands were met. The claim was reported on January 23, with an initial ransom deadline reported for January 24. ICICI Bank did not publicly confirm the alleged breach. The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) penalised ICICI Bank ₹97.80 lakh on April 29, 2025 for non-compliance with guidelines regarding its Cyber Security Framework in Banks, KYC rules, and card-issuance regulations. In April 2024, ICICI Bank's digital channels incorrectly mapped about 17,000 newly issued credit cards to the wrong users. Customers reported that the iMobile Pay app was displaying other customers' card details due to a technical glitch, including full card numbers and CVVs, the security codes used for card-not-present transactions. The bank said the affected cards represented about 0.1 per cent of its credit card portfolio. ICICI Bank acknowledged the exposure of credit-card information, blocked the affected cards and began issuing replacements. It said no misuse of the cards had been reported and promised to compensate customers for any financial loss resulting from the incident. The bank did not report confirmed customer losses arising from the error. The incident was a significant exposure of sensitive card information, but the bank's statement did not establish that the exposed details had been used fraudulently. 4. Alleged PNB data leaks In November 2021, cybersecurity firm CyberX9 alleged that a vulnerability in a Punjab National Bank (PNB) server had potentially exposed the personal and financial information of around 180 million customers for approximately seven months, according to media reports. PNB denied that its systems had been breached or customer data stolen. It said it had checked the relevant information systems and found no breach of the kind alleged. In February 2018, details associated with around 10,000 PNB debit and credit card accounts was offered for sale online. The information reportedly included cardholder names, expiry dates, personal identification numbers (PINs) and card verification values (CVVs). Singapore-based cybersecurity firm CloudSek detected the data and alerted the bank through a government agency. The bank denied the claim and said its security infrastructure is robust. 5. 300 cooperative banks and regional rural banks: July-August 2024 A ransomware attack on C-Edge Technologies, a banking technology service provider, disrupted payment services at nearly 300 cooperative banks and regional rural banks. Ransomware is malicious software that locks or encrypts systems, often to demand payment. The National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) temporarily isolated C-Edge from its retail payment network to prevent the attack from spreading. The affected institutions accounted for around 0.5 per cent of India's payment-system volumes, according to a Reuters report. NPCI's precautionary action temporarily prevented customers of banks served by C-Edge from accessing affected payment systems. By August 1, the banks were back online. NPCI said a forensic review found that the ransomware had not spread to the lenders' own systems and remained confined to C-Edge's infrastructure.

item.title: JSW Steel Q2 results preview: Adj. PAT could grow 60-110% YoY, say analysts
item.description: Elara Capital said that steel demand remained resilient, supported by channel restocking ahead of expected price hikes.
item.content:encoded:
Home / Markets / News / JSW Steel Q2 results preview: Adj. PAT could grow 60-110% YoY, say analysts

JSW Steel Q2 results preview: Adj. PAT could grow 60-110% YoY, say analysts Elara Capital said that steel demand remained resilient, supported by channel restocking ahead of expected price hikes.

JSW Steel, JSW (Photo: Reuters)

SI Reporter New Delhi 3 min read Last Updated : Oct 22 2026 | 2:49 PM IST

Listen to This Article

JSW Steel Q2 results preview : Integrated steel producer JSW Steel could report strong growth in net profit for the July-September quarter (Q2) of the financial year 2026-27 (FY27), helped by firmer prices, limiting the usual seasonal pressure on profitability.   Domestic hot-rolled coil (HRC) and cold-rolled coil (CRC) prices remained firm in Q2FY27, up ~21-22 per cent YoY and ~3–4 per cent QoQ, respectively. The primary rebar and semis prices declined in the second quarter, falling ~3 per cent QoQ and ~1 per cent QoQ, respectively.   Elara Capital said that steel demand remained resilient, supported by channel restocking ahead of expected price hikes, healthy demand from the pipe sector, improving construction activity following a patchy monsoon, and strong auto demand, particularly for galvanized products.

Against this backdrop, JSW Steel is expected to post a 60-110 per cent year-on-year (YoY) rise in the adjusted net profit for the quarter under review, while its net sales could grow in double digits.   JSW Steel Q2 preview Here's what brokerages expect: Also Read

Kotak Institutional Equities (KIE) According to KIE, the net sales could rise 23.2 per cent year-on-year (YoY) and 17.6 per cent quarter-on-quarter (QoQ) to ₹54,888.4 crore while the adjusted profit could see a 110.7 per cent YoY and 7 per cent QoQ rise to ₹4,965.5 crore.   The brokerage said it expects JSW Steel's India operations (ex-BPSL) to report volumes of ~7 million tons (+13.2 per cent YoY and +17 per cent QoQ), with JVML volumes at ~1.1 million tons. "We build in seasonal price weakness with standalone steel realizations to decrease by 1.1 per cent QoQ (+27 per cent YoY)," it said.

Further, it estimates India operations' EBITDA/ton to decrease to ₹13,744/ton (+26 per cent YoY and -10.1 per cent QoQ) led by QoQ lower realizations/higher coking coal costs during the quarter.   Motilal Oswal Financial Services (MOFSL) According to MOFSL, the adjusted PAT could rise 60 per cent YoY to ₹3300 crore on the back of a 7 per cent growth in sales in Q2 FY27.   The brokerage said that a flat-to-marginal rise in NSR will support earnings. Meanwhile, sales volume is expected to remain healthy over capacity ramp-up.   Guidance on capex status and demand/pricing outlook along with commentary on cost inflation will be key monitorables, said MOFSL analysts.

Home / Markets / IPO / Jio Platforms IPO: Retail quota full, subscribed 3.47 times on day two

Jio Platforms IPO: Retail quota full, subscribed 3.47 times on day two The $3.2 billion IPO drew bids for 3.47 times the shares on offer on its second day, led by qualified institutional buyers whose quota was subscribed 9.42 times, exchange data showed

Image: Bloomberg

Reuters Mumbai 1 min read Last Updated : Oct 22 2026 | 12:13 PM IST

Listen to This Article

Appetite for the $3.2 billion IPO of billionaire Mukesh Ambani's Jio Platforms kept building on Thursday, its second day of public bidding, with orders at 3.47 times the shares up for grabs and the retail portion now fully subscribed, exchange data showed. In what is set to be India's largest IPO and the first by Reliance in 20 years, the listing is a key plank of Ambani's long-term vision to turn Reliance from an oil-and-chemicals giant into an "everything company" spanning consumer, retail and technology. Institutional investors have led demand, with qualified institutional buyers bidding for 9.42 times their quota, exchange data showed. Retail investors, for whom around a third of the issue is reserved, covered their own portion in full by the first two hours of bidding on day two.
